numerical_failure.observed_behavior: SGD models (primarily SGDOneClassSVM) use only the loss/error (via Avg. loss/`sumloss`) as the stopping criterion when `tol != None`, so training stops prematurely (e.g., “stops after 6 epochs, the initial epoch, plus the 5 for stopping tolerance”). The verbose output can show Avg. loss as 0.0 while the full objective (with regularization) is different, and convergence is misleading. In the PR example, objective and Avg. loss diverge, with Avg. loss reported as 0.000000 while “Objective: -0.121162” is still not the same metric used for convergence before the fix.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: When `tol != None`, the stopping/convergence check should use the full optimization objective with regularization (i.e., the objective sum that includes regularization/weight decay terms), not just the loss/error without penalty. The fix is described as: “use objective instead of loss for convergence in SGD” and “Now uses full objective with regularization, instead of just loss.”
trigger_conditions: SGDOneClassSVM (primarily affected) with default early stopping criteria when `tol != None` (the issue title: “does not converge with default stopping criteria (stops prematurely)”).

Presence of penalty/regularization terms so that loss can be near 0.0 while the full objective differs (the issue notes loss used for stopping/reporting doesn’t account for full model formula/regularization).
Execution where verbose output indicates Avg. loss can be 0.0 and convergence/termination happens too early (noted as occurring “almost always” after ~6 epochs).

oracle_clues: The issue states the convergence check uses the “used loss” which is “not actual loss, but only error,” and that this “doesn’t account for the full model formula/regularization.”
The doc/whats_new entry states: “Before this fix, only the loss function without penalty was used as convergence check. Now, the full objective with regularization is used.”

The PR code change computes an objective accumulator: `cur_loss_val = loss.cy_loss(y, p)`; `sumloss += cur_loss_val`; and then (for non-PA1/PA2) `objective_sum += cur_loss_val` and if `penalty_type > 0` adds regularization terms via `alpha` (the continuation is truncated in the passage).
The issue observes the problem “almost always stops after 6 epochs, the initial epoch, plus the 5 for stopping tolerance.”

numerical_characteristics.tolerance: tol=1e-3 (test uses tol=1e-3); also tol=None used as a workaround (slows optimization); convergence differs when tol != None (premature stopping)
category_specific_evidence: SGDOneClassSVM does not converge with default early stopping criteria because the used loss for stopping is not the actual loss/objective, so it can reach 0.0 easily and then increase as the model converges; pay attention to bias term to gauge convergence.
Optimization almost always stops after 6 epochs (initial epoch plus the 5 for stopping tolerance); number of epochs for stopping tolerance cannot be changed.
The problem does not manifest with toy data (small dimensional) because 6 epochs is likely enough for convergence to a satisfactory solution.
Expected: model convergence criteria works adequately (especially important for learning_rate='adaptive') and model reaches convergence.
Actual: optimization stops prematurely, usually after 6 epochs; training log shows Avg. loss values around ~0.000088 to ~0.000193 over epochs 1–5 (example snippet).

Fix description: when tol != None, only the loss without penalty was used as convergence check; now the full objective with regularization is used; full objective includes regularization for regression/classification and the intercept term for one-class SVM.
PR/test criterion: non-regression test asserts that model.n_iter_ > 6 when SGDOneClassSVM is run with max_iter=100, tol=1e-3, learning_rate='constant', eta0=1e-3 on iris.data.
Workaround mentioned: use tol=None with manual epoch limit (max_iter), but that slows the optimization.
Test vs reference: uses SGDOneClassSVM with max_iter=20000 and tol=None and compares against liblinear OneClassSVM (kernel='linear', tol=1e-6).
reproduction_risks: The premature stopping is tied to tol != None; if tol is None, use of the correct stopping criterion may not reproduce the premature convergence behavior.

Stopping behavior is characterized in terms of epoch/iteration count: it often stops after ~6 epochs (initial epoch + 5 for stopping tolerance); reproductions that do not observe/record the epoch/iteration count may miss the differing behavior.
The stopping check previously used only the raw loss (error), which can be ~0.0; reproductions that don’t monitor the reported 'loss' vs the full objective may not align with the bug mechanism.
Reproduction should ensure the bias/intercept term is present/handled (noted as important for gauging convergence).
